newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian Interior Ministry bans demonstrations.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian Interior Ministry bans demonstrations.

text.p: Cambodia's Interior Ministry has slapped a temporary ban on street protests following a deadly grenade attack on an opposition rally in the capital last month, a top official said on Wednesday.
"From today, the Ministry of Interior will not give permission to anyone to hold demonstrations as the (political) situation is not good," co-Interior Minister You Hokry told Reuters.

The minister, reached by telephone, said interior officials had been directed to reject requests for demonstrations. "The ministry will give permission again if the situation becomes better," he added.
Co-Minister of Interior Sar Kheng could not be reached for comment.

The decision follows a March 30 grenade attack on a demonstration led by opposition Khmer Nation Party (KNP) leader and apparent target Sam Rainsy, who narrowly escaped injury from blasts that left up to 19 people dead and more than 100 injured.

The Interior Ministry has launched an investigation into the attack outside parliament, but many people, including First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, have expressed doubts it would bring those responsible to justice.
Local human rights groups and the KNP condemned the ministry's decision as unconstitutional.
"The ban is against democracy and is also not constitutional. The ban is not good. If there is no opinion there is no democracy," KNP Secretary-General Khieu Rada told Reuters on Wednesday.
